Interface IuOidcProviderReference

public interface IuOidcProviderReference
Provides application resources to the endpoints of an OpenID Provider.

One thing an integration implements, rather than a collaborator per seam. A servlet, a JAX-RS application, or whatever else stands the provider up binds what it has — a session handler, a data store, a way to authenticate, whatever reads registrations and identity — and hands over a single reference. Every endpoint reads through it, so adding an endpoint doesn't add a constructor argument, and so two endpoints cannot be wired to disagree about who this provider is.

This is not intended to be a structural interface. An implementation declares it explicitly and overrides what it uses; everything a deployment doesn't reach for refuses by default rather than answering something plausible, so a missing binding fails where it is needed and says which one it was.

What isn't here

No JSON. An integration depends on IuConfig for itself, and configures both the JSON its endpoints answer with and the claim adapters a stored grant round-trips through. What this hands the provider is typed or opaque, never a document, and the one thing the provider does publish verbatim — a UserInfo claims document — comes rendered from the claims source.

  • Method Details

    • getConfiguration

      IuOidcProviderConfiguration getConfiguration()
      Gets this provider's own configuration.

      Read afresh on every use rather than captured, so a change takes effect on the next request. An implementation backed by a caching configuration source is what bounds how often that read costs anything.

      Returns:
      IuOidcProviderConfiguration

      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the deployment binds none

    • getAuthorizationDetailsSource

      default IuOidcAuthorizationDetailsSource getAuthorizationDetailsSource()
      Gets the source that decides what a client's requested authorization details release to an end user.

      Answers null by default, which releases nothing. A deployment that grants nothing this way needs no binding.

      Returns:
      IuOidcAuthorizationDetailsSource

    • getSessionHandler

      default edu.iu.session.IuSessionHandler getSessionHandler()
      Gets the session handler an authorization request is held in across the round trip to the identity provider.

      Must be a handler of its own. One shared with the authentication mechanism would have each overwrite the other's cookie.

      Returns:
      IuSessionHandler
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the deployment binds none

    • getDataStore

      default edu.iu.IuDataStore getDataStore()
      Gets the store authorization codes and refresh tokens are filed in.

      Typically the same store the deployment keeps authenticated sessions in, rather than a second connection to the same server. What is filed there is encrypted to a key the reference itself carries, so the store holds nothing it can read.

      Returns:
      IuDataStore
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the deployment binds none

    • getAuthenticatedPrincipal

      default IuOidcAuthenticatedPrincipal getAuthenticatedPrincipal(edu.iu.IuRequestAttributes attributes)
      Gets the principal an identity provider has established for a request.

      However a deployment authenticates — SAML, Kerberos, a container login — this is where the result arrives, and nothing about the mechanism reaches the provider. An unauthenticated request is the ordinary first pass rather than a failure, and an implementation reports it either by answering null or by refusing the lookup; both read the same way.

      Parameters:
      attributes - incoming request attributes, which is how a session is found
      Returns:
      IuOidcAuthenticatedPrincipal; null if nothing is established

    • getCertificateAuthorityVerifier

      default edu.iu.pki.IuPkiVerifier getCertificateAuthorityVerifier(edu.iu.pki.IuCertificateAuthority certificateAuthority)
      Gets a verifier for one client's registered certificate authority.

      Which registration warrants which kind of verification is the provider's — a registration carrying a revocation list is an authority, one without is a bare or self-signed key — and so is what a failure means. What does the verifying is the deployment's, since every implementation of IuPkiVerifier lives in a module a library has no business compiling against.

      Parameters:
      certificateAuthority - authority a client's certificate must chain to
      Returns:
      IuPkiVerifier
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the deployment binds none, which refuses every client authenticating by a CA-issued certificate

    • getSelfSignedVerifier

      default edu.iu.pki.IuPkiVerifier getSelfSignedVerifier(edu.iu.crypt.WebKey jwk)
      Gets a verifier for a client's own self-signed key.

      Separate from getCertificateAuthorityVerifier(IuCertificateAuthority) because the two are built from different things — an authority from the registration, a self-signed key from the key itself — and because a provider knows which it needs before it needs one.

      Parameters:
      jwk - key carrying the self-signed certificate to trust
      Returns:
      IuPkiVerifier
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the deployment binds none, which refuses every client registered with a self-signed certificate

    • isProduction

      default boolean isProduction()
      Determines whether this is a production deployment.

      Gates impersonation, which is honored only outside production and only for a principal holding one of the endpoint's backdoor roles. Defaults to true, so a deployment that says nothing is treated as production and a forgotten binding closes the backdoor rather than opening it.

      Returns:
      true if this deployment is a production one
